I'm 46 yr old female who was diagnosed with T2D at 26. For 20 years, I've been taking Metformin. It just recently stopped working, my A1c shot up from 6.8 to 9 something; I never noticed the shift because my eye appointment was normal and I'd been regularly exercising, just not testing because I fell into a pattern of thinking everything was fine. I felt ill last week and one night and took my blood glucose reading: 230. It was shocking. This is a gentle reminder to test frequently. I found myself unable to lower my blood glucose since then, even after going to extremes in eating very little and seeing increases of 50 points or more... with no carbs and flooding myself with water. I thought going keto again or intermittent fasting would save me, but after some of the scariest few days of my life, I realized I had to change my medication. When you see the reviews here and the class action lawsuit alerts from various diabetic medications in general on TV commercials, it shapes your perception in such a way that you're fearful of trying a new diabetes medication. I took my first injection of Trulicity last Friday without incident. In fact, I was able to eat lightly like a normal healthy person and not feel much hunger... even as I'd been eating under 800 calories to try to move the needle on my own the last few days, afraid of going into a diabetic coma with those high numbers that peaked at 260. I've been eating mindfully still, and the increases 2 hours later have been 6 points and 10 points, not 70 and 90. Trulicity has given me such great peace of mind. I hope I don't develop any issues like those noted in the warnings and the loud box warning because I don't have insurance right now. For now, I feel like I won't die tomorrow and I'm taking this one day at a time full of hope and so grateful to the makers of this drug.
